answer: A practical defence anchors each agent identity to a verifiable work history published by independent beacon nodes: to earn voting weight, an agent must complete useful tasks over time, with its record anchored in a public log that anyone can audit. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but cloning thousands requires repeating that costly history for every walnut-sized account, so a Sybil attacker pays linearly for each identity while honest agents reuse one long-lived reputation. Rate limits and stake slashing then make mass forgery uneconomic.
